{{Short description|American mathematician (1899–1987)}}
'''Ruel Vance Churchill''' (12 December 1899 – 31 October 1987) was an American mathematician and author known for writing three widely used textbooks on [[applied mathematics]].<ref>[http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/ruel-vance-churchill/memorial Ruel Vance Churchill, Faculty History Project, U. of Michigan, Ann Arbor]</ref>

Churchill was born in [[Akron, Indiana]] in 1899, and in 1922 he received his undergraduate degree from the [[University of Chicago]]. In 1929 he received his PhD from the [[University of Michigan]] under [[George Yuri Rainich|George Rainich]] with thesis ''On the Geometry of the Riemann Tensor''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=5288}}</ref> He spent his entire career as a member of the U. of Michigan mathematics faculty and retired in 1965 as professor emeritus.<ref>[http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/ruel-vance-churchill University of Michigan: Faculty Member Resources]</ref> His doctoral students include [[Earl D. Rainville]].

Churchill died in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]] in 1987.

==Books==
*Complex Variables and Applications, McGraw-Hill, 1st edition 1948, 2nd edition 1960, The 3rd (1974) and later editions were co-authored with James Ward Brown
*Fourier Series and Boundary Value Problems, McGraw-Hill, 1941, 2nd edition 1963<ref>{{cite journal|author=Levinson, N.|authorlink=Norman Levinson|title=Review: ''Fourier Series and Boundary Values Problems'' by R. V. Churchill|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=47|issue=7|pages=538–539|url=http://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1941-47-07/S0002-9904-1941-07480-X/S0002-9904-1941-07480-X.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1941-07480-x|year=1941|doi-access=free}}</ref>
*Modern Operational Mathematics in Engineering, McGraw-Hill, 1944<ref>{{cite journal|author=Camp, Glen D.|title=Review: ''Modern Operational Methods in Engineering'' by R. V. Churchill|journal=National Mathematics Magazine|date=October 1945|pages=44–46|doi=10.2307/3029973|volume=20|issue=1|jstor=3029973|hdl=2027/mdp.39015000983000|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
*Operational Mathematics, McGraw-Hill, 1958, 2nd edition of the 1944 book but with a new title, 3rd edition 1972
